events.description:
💜 On the Day of the Dead, we remember, honor, and hold space for those we’ve lost. 🕊️

Grief looks different for everyone. Whether you’re remembering a loved one, navigating feelings of loss, or finding your way through a difficult time, give yourself permission to feel, reflect, and heal at your own pace. There’s no right or wrong way to grieve, and you don’t have to go through it alone. 💜

🐾 Looking for support? Join Getting Through Grief, an ongoing UW Counseling Center Fall group where you can connect with others who understand the challenges of grief and loss.

📅 Thursdays | 9–10:20 AM via Zoom

You deserve support, connection, and space to heal.

Visit our website @uwcounseling for more information and details

👀 Hey Pre-Optometry Club! We are so excited to announce our next event! We will be hosting an Optometrist Q&A session with our guest speaker, Dr. Jason Chau! 

Join us on Monday, November 23rd at 7:00 PM in STC 0020 for an opportunity to learn more about the field of optometry, hear about Dr. Chau’s journey from optometry school to clinical practice, and gain insight into what it’s like to own and operate an optometry clinic!

Grab your friends, get your questions ready, and come join us for an evening of great conversations, food, and refreshments!

🔗Sign up using the link in our bio :)

Get to know our speaker:

Dr. Jason Chau is an optometrist and Clinic Director at Innovation Eye Clinic, a modern optometry practice located in downtown Kitchener, Ontario. He earned his Doctor of Optometry (OD) degree from the University of Waterloo and has a special interest in dry eye therapy, myopia management, and orthokeratology (Ortho-K). After graduating, Dr. Chau gained experience in ocular research at the Centre for Ocular Research & Education (CORE). In 2023, he opened Innovation Eye Clinic with the goal of providing personalized, patient-centred eye care through advanced diagnostic technology and evidence-based treatments. Dr. Chau is passionate about patient education and combining innovative approaches to eye care with meaningful patient relationships.

We can’t wait to see you there! 💙👁️

events.title: Accessibility Audit - Wallingford
events.description:
UAG welcomes any and all interested students to join us for our Accessibility (Walk) Audit of the Wallingford neighborhood of Seattle. We will be convening in the parking lot of the Burke museum at the start time, then we will travel as a group to the start location.
We will be using an app to record the infrastructure accessibility of a section of the neighborhood. This data can then be used for awareness and advocacy purposes, as well as being integrated into a tool that allows people with mobility impairments plan urban routes that accommodate their specific accessibility needs.
Mostly, these audits are about raising awareness about urban accessibility and enjoying a walk with other great people. Volunteer hours are provided to all participants.
